English for real life · Lesson 3

Feelings 💛

Say more than just good and bad. A2–B1 speaking lesson based on a video about emotions — less writing, more talking.

01 · warm-up

Let's talk about the video ☕

7 min

Answer naturally. You don't need perfect sentences — let's get talking first.

Useful to describe — полезно описывать · precisely — точно, конкретно · instead of — вместо · small differences in intensity — небольшие различия в степени выраженности чувства.

1. How are you today? How has your day been so far? — Как ты сегодня? Как проходит твой день?
2. How has your week been? Has anything new or interesting happened? Tell me about it.
3. Looking at the video, what do you think today's lesson is about?
4. Do you think it's useful to describe your feelings in English more precisely, instead of only saying good or bad? Why? — Как думаешь, полезно ли описывать свои чувства на английском точнее, вместо того чтобы говорить только «хорошо» или «плохо»? Почему?
5. Did you like this new blogger? Was he easier to understand, harder, or about the same as Miss Honey from our second lesson?
6. Did you answer his questions or practise the dialogues, or did you skip those parts?
7. Tell me 3 things you remember from the video.

Active phrases · Finish the thought

Complete each sentence with a feeling and a detail. Several answers are possible. Say your answers out loud.

  1. I'm feeling ______ today because ______.
  2. I feel a little ______ when ______.
  3. I'm kind of ______ about ______.
  4. It makes me feel really ______ when someone ______.
  5. I felt extremely ______ the last time ______.
  6. I'm proud of myself when ______.
  7. I feel overwhelmed when ______, but it helps when ______.
  8. Listening to / watching ______ makes me feel ______.
Small but important · -ED or -ING? ✨

-ED = how a person feels. Обычно описывает эмоцию, которую человек испытывает.

  • I'm excited about the trip. — Я в восторге от поездки.
  • I'm bored. — Мне скучно.
  • She was embarrassed. — Ей было неловко / она смутилась.
  • We were surprised by the news. — Мы удивились этой новости.
  • He feels overwhelmed. — Он чувствует себя перегруженным.

-ING = what causes the feeling. Обычно так описываем событие, ситуацию, фильм или новость, которые вызывают эмоцию.

  • The trip is exciting. — Поездка захватывающая / очень интересная.
  • The film is boring. — Фильм скучный.
  • The situation was embarrassing. — Ситуация была неловкой.
  • The news was surprising. — Новость была удивительной / неожиданной.
  • This week has been exhausting. — Эта неделя была изматывающей.

Compare: I'm bored because the lesson is boring. — Мне скучно, потому что урок скучный.
I'm interested in this topic because it's interesting. — Мне интересна эта тема, потому что она интересная.
I'm confused because the instructions are confusing. — Я запуталась, потому что инструкции запутанные.

Quick rule: person + usually -ED (bored, excited, interested); thing/situation + often -ING (boring, exciting, interesting). Это полезное правило для большинства повседневных примеров.

Task A · Complete the sentences

Choose from the vocabulary box. Use each word once if possible.

  1. I'd prepared for the interview for weeks, so when they cancelled it ten minutes before it started, I felt really ______.
  2. There were so many deadlines, messages and errands that I didn't know what to do first. I felt completely ______.
  3. I couldn't understand the instructions, and everyone else seemed to know what was happening. I was totally ______.
  4. I'd been waiting for the exam results all morning. When I saw that I'd passed, I felt incredibly ______.
  5. I dropped my drink in a quiet café and everyone turned to look at me. I was so ______.
  6. My friend stayed with me and helped me solve the problem. I felt really ______ to have someone like her.
  7. I'd practised the presentation for days, and it went even better than I expected. I felt ______ of myself.
  8. The app kept crashing, and I couldn't finish the form before the deadline. I was getting really ______.
Show answers

1 disappointed · 2 overwhelmed · 3 confused · 4 relieved · 5 embarrassed · 6 grateful · 7 proud · 8 frustrated

Task B · Choose the best option

  1. You've wanted to see your favourite band for years and you finally have tickets. (excited / disappointed / confused)
  2. Your friend says “Don't worry, I've already taken care of it,” and the problem is solved. (relieved / frustrated / embarrassed)
  3. You studied hard, but your result was much lower than you expected. (grateful / disappointed / proud)
  4. You have three big tasks to finish today and no idea where to start. (overwhelmed / relaxed / excited)
  5. You are about to speak in front of 100 people for the first time. (nervous / calm / grateful)
  6. Someone compliments your work and says you did an excellent job. (proud / confused / stressed)
Show answers

excited · relieved · disappointed · overwhelmed · nervous · proud

  1. I feel frustrated when ______, especially if ______.
  2. I was relieved the last time ______.

  4. I felt proud of myself when ______.
  5. I get nervous before ______, but I feel better when ______.
04 · talk about you

How would you react? ✨

15 min

Choose questions at random. Explain your feeling, say why, and describe what you would do next.

1. How would you react if your favourite celebrity followed you on Instagram? 📱
2. How would you react if you got a message saying, “I've booked us a trip to Japan!”? ✈️
3. How would you react if you suddenly became famous on TikTok? 📸
4. How would you react if someone pushed in front of you in a queue? 😤
5. What would you feel if your best friend moved to another country and you couldn't visit them? 🌍
6. How would you react if you had to say goodbye to someone you loved? 💔
7. What would you feel if you realised you'd been talking to someone for five minutes with food stuck in your teeth? 🥲
8. How would you react if you accidentally liked a photo your crush posted three years ago? 📱💀
9. How would you react if you woke up and everyone around you suddenly started speaking a language you didn't understand? 🌎
10. How would you react if you woke up with bright green hair and had no idea how it happened? 💚
11. What would you feel if you had to wear the same outfit every day for a year? 👗
Keep the conversation going — choose a follow-up:
  • Why would you feel that way?
  • What would you do next?
  • Would you tell anyone about it?
  • Would you laugh or cry?
  • Would you forgive the person?
  • Would you try to hide your feelings?
  • Would you react differently if it happened in public?
  • Have you ever experienced anything similar?
  • What would be the worst possible reaction?
  • What would you do if you couldn't control your emotions?

⭐ Bonus grammar · keep it simple

should have + V3 = “мне надо было сделать, но я не сделал(а)”.
I should have studied earlier.

would have + V3 = “я бы сделал(а) это в прошлом, если бы условия были другими”.
I would have called you, but I lost my phone.

would + verb = “я бы…” в воображаемой ситуации.
If I weren't afraid, I would travel more.

Say one: Last weekend I should have ______. / If I weren't afraid, I would ______.

05 · video questions & extra

Questions from the video 🎧

6 min

Answer using one of today's sentence patterns. Try to use an intensity word, too.

1. How are you?
2. How are you feeling?
3. Why are you so happy?
4. What's wrong?
5. Are you nervous? When do you get nervous?
6. Do you feel stressed? Do you feel stressed right now?
7. What is your favourite emotion?
Useful sentence patterns from the video
  • I'm + emotion: I'm nervous.
  • I feel + emotion: I feel sad.
  • I'm feeling + emotion: I'm feeling tired today.
  • I feel + emotion + because…: I feel happy because I'm with my friends.
  • It makes me feel + emotion: Music makes me feel relaxed.

HOMEWORK · before next lesson

Watch Inside Out 🎬

at home

Film: Inside Out (2015) — watch here

Your mission: tell me the name of each emotion and describe what they are like.

How to learn with films and series

  1. Watch in small chunks. Treat 10–15 minutes as a full mini-lesson. Pause when you need to.
  2. Try without Russian subtitles first. Focus on the situation, faces, actions and words you recognise. You don't need to understand every word.
  3. Use English subtitles if you need them. If watching without subtitles feels stressful, keep English subtitles on. The goal is to learn, not to suffer.
  4. Don't translate everything. Look up a word only when it seems useful or you really want to know what it means.
  5. Write down 5–7 words or phrases you like. Choose expressions you could imagine using yourself, not every unfamiliar word.
  6. Work with your phrases. Check the meaning, say each phrase aloud, make your own sentence and review it later.
  7. Come ready to talk. Next lesson, tell me the names of the emotions in the film and describe each one in English.
Remember: Watching helps you understand, but pausing, noticing useful phrases, saying them aloud and reviewing them helps you remember. Also, learn the vocabulary from today's Quizlet set.
